SharedFlowBundle.name: ISAM-Common-ExtractClientCert
SharedFlowBundle.Description:
Reusable building block: resolves the caller's client certificate into canonical variables, so every SAML/JWT type embeds the same values in its request to ISAM instead of each type reading a header directly.
NAMING: every output variable here lives under isam.client.cert.*, never bare client.*. client is a RESERVED Apigee system variable prefix (client.ip, client.port, etc., all platform-populated and read-only); an earlier version of this bundle used client.cert.* and every write to it was silently rejected, no matter how it was written (native AssignVariable/Template, a JavaScript context.setVariable() -- neither worked, both were writing to a read-only prefix). Confirmed via trace: a rejected write shows a not-equals marker on the variable meaning "could not be assigned, read-only". Do not reintroduce a client.* variable name in this bundle.
OUTPUT variables: isam.client.cert.base64 string, the client's X.509 certificate as BARE base64 -- no "-----BEGIN CERTIFICATE -----"/"-----END CERTIFICATE -----" armor, no internal line-wrap whitespace, exactly the form ISAM's request expects. Null if the caller presented no certificate through either source below. isam.client.cert.subject.dn string, the cert's subject Distinguished Name, plain text. isam.client.cert.issuer.dn string, the cert's issuer Distinguished Name, plain text. isam.client.cert.subject.dn.base64 the same subject DN, base64-encoded (this, not the plain-text form above, is what goes in the request to ISAM). isam.client.cert.issuer.dn.base64 the same issuer DN, base64-encoded.
The four DN variables are only populated via source 1 below (tls.client.s.dn / tls.client.i.dn) -- the header fallback never carries a pre-parsed DN, only the raw cert, so all four stay null whenever isam.client.cert.base64 was resolved from request.header.X-Client-Cert instead.
Two sources, tried in order: 1. tls.client.raw.cert (PEM) / tls.client.s.dn / tls.client.i.dn -- what Apigee itself captured during a two-way TLS handshake on its own VirtualHost. This is the authoritative source when mutual TLS terminates AT Apigee. These are ONLY populated if the VirtualHost is configured for client auth: - Edge Private/Public Cloud: the VirtualHost's SSLInfo needs ClientAuthEnabled set to true, plus a TrustStore holding the accepted client CA chain. - Apigee X/hybrid: the environment's TLS config has propagateTLSInformation.clientProperties = true. That configuration lives on the VirtualHost/environment, not in any proxy or shared flow bundle, so it will not show up in this repo -- if isam.client.cert.base64 keeps coming back null in an environment where you expect mTLS at the gateway, check that config first, not this bundle's policies (and see the NAMING note above if you see a value in trace with a not-equals marker next to it, rather than a genuinely-null variable). tls.client. raw.cert comes back PEM-armored (with BEGIN/END lines and line-wrap whitespace); stripping that down to the bare base64 stored in isam.client.cert.base64 is done by JS-Extract-Client-Cert-Strip, a plain JavaScript policy (resources/jsc/strip-pem-armor.js). The DN variables above are still native AssignVariable (in AM-Extract-Client-Cert-TLS) -- only the cert-stripping half moved to JavaScript. That move was made after 3 different native message-template/replaceAll() attempts (a single combined regex, single- vs double-backslash \s variants, and a version split across 3 chained AssignVariable policy steps) all still came back as unevaluated literal text in trace; those were real bugs in their own right (Apigee message templates disallow spaces anywhere in a function expression, even inside a quoted literal, and \s needs to be written \\s), worth knowing about independently, but NOT the actual reason the certificate itself never made it into the request -- that was the client.* naming collision described above, which affected the cert-stripping output variable regardless of which technique (native or JavaScript) tried to write it. 2. request.header.X-Client-Cert -- a certificate forwarded by an upstream device (a load balancer or reverse proxy in front of Apigee) that terminates mutual TLS itself, expected already in bare base64 (no PEM armor, no URL-encoding). Only used as a fallback when tls.client.raw.cert is unset, i.e. Apigee did not itself terminate mTLS for this request.
Every type-specific shared flow (ISAM-SAML-Light, ISAM-SAML-User, ISAM-SAML-TP, ISAM-SAML-Technical, ISAM-JWT-SAML, ISAM-JWT-Token) calls this one via FlowCallout early in its flow, before building its request to ISAM, and reads these variables afterwards.
